To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we designed a protein scaffold that can be used to attach small proteins and nucleic acids to a large, symmetric scaffold, and then use the attached small protein or nucleic acids as targets for single-particle cryogenic electron microscopy (cryoEM).
a small protein of typical size in cells can be visualized by cryo- EM when it is attached rigidly and symmetrically on a designed scaffolds.
we have developed a protein scaffold that can be used to display a small protein for structural analysis by cryo- EM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of protein scaffolds to facilitate structural studies of smaller proteins.
the design of a protein scaffolding system that can be used to display small proteins for cryo- electron microscopy.
the development of a protein design approach to create a protein scaffold for cryo- EM imaging of small protein molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown how a small protein can be attached to a designed scaffold to allow its structure to be visualized by cryo-electron microscopic imaging.
we demonstrate the feasibility of using designed protein scaffolds to enable cryo-EM analysis of small proteins, and the method may be useful for imaging a range of cellular proteins.
we have demonstrated the ability to visualize a small protein (DARpin) attached to a larger protein (D4-2) at near-atomic resolution by single-particle electron microscopy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed a system that allows for the visualization of small proteins by cryo-electron microcopy.
we have developed a method to visualize a protein smaller than the theoretical resolution limit for cryo- EM, by using a rigidly arranged protein scaffold.
a protein much below the size limit of 50 kiloDaltons (kDa) is now amenable to cryo-EM when it is displayed on a rigid, designed scaffolding system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a protein of typical size can be made amenable to cryo-EM by attaching it to a designed scaffold.
a small protein of approximately 17 kDa can be imaged in near-atomic detail by cryo- EM when attached to a rigid and symmetric protein scaffold.
small proteins can be visualized at near-atomic resolution by cryo-Em if they are displayed on a rigid, symmetrical scaffold.
